newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C Bank offers one-day rrp at 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila C Bank offers one-day rrp at 30 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Monday it started offering one-day reverse repos at 30 percent.
It said it will accept placements until noon today.
Traders said the Central Bank was forced to raise its rate after selling dollars heavily in the morning at 26.40 pesos when volume rose to $209 million.
Last week, the Central Bank was offering one-day reverse repo at 24 percent.
The last time the Central Bank raised its rate to 30 percent was in March 1995 in the aftermath of Mexico's financial crisis.
A Singapore-based newspaper on Monday quoted Finance Secretary Roberto De Ocampo saying the Philippine peso may devalue against the U.S. dollar.
But a Central Bank official said De Ocampo had been misquoted. De Ocampo was not immediately available for comment.
